corrected_value.title: Association between genes, stressful childhood events and processing bias in depression vulnerable individuals

decisions.quote: In line with other intermediate phenotype findings, our conceptual replication partly supports earlier G x E findings, linking automatic biased processing of emotional information to genetic risk profiles and childhood trauma [ 10 , 11 , 14 , 16 – 22 ]. We extended these findings to a naturalistic sample of (previously) depressed individuals and specifically found that automatic avoidance tendencies of sad faces might be one of the intermediate phenotypes mediating the relationship between genes and depression vulnerability. However, the specific pattern of results was (partly) unexpected.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly frames its 'conceptual replication' around earlier gene x environment (G x E) intermediate-phenotype studies linking biased emotional processing to genetic risk and childhood trauma, citing [20, 21, 22] in the Introduction and [10, 11, 14, 16-22] (which includes Reference 20, Vrijsen et al., 2014) in the Discussion verdict. The blind coder's alternative target, Seidel et al. (2010) [42], was a non-genetic study of behavioral tendencies in depression used alongside clinical experience and depression theory to motivate expecting avoidance of negative (sad, angry) faces in the vulnerable subgroup, rather than the G x E intermediate-phenotype claim defined by the authors as their conceptual replication.

decisions.reason: Following the codebook's overall-verdict and set-verdict rules, the authors explicitly conclude that their conceptual replication 'partly supports earlier G x E findings, linking automatic biased processing of emotional information to genetic risk profiles and childhood trauma [ 10 , 11 , 14 , 16 – 22 ]' (which includes Reference 20, Vrijsen et al., 2014) while noting that 'the specific pattern of results was (partly) unexpected' (S/Lg-carriers with childhood trauma avoided sad faces more than LaLa homozygotes with trauma, but LaLa homozygotes without trauma also unexpectedly avoided sad faces more than LaLa homozygotes with trauma, S/Lg-carriers with vs. without trauma did not differ, and no interaction held for angry, happy, or neutral faces). The blind coder's 'failed' verdict pertained only to the angry-face expectation from Seidel et al. [42], not to Vrijsen et al. [20].

decisions.quote: Depression risk genes in combination with childhood events have been associated with biased processing as an intermediate phenotype for depression. The aim of the present conceptual replication study was to investigate the role of biased automatic approach-avoidance tendencies as a candidate intermediate phenotype for depression, in the context of genes (5-HTTLPR polymorphism) and childhood trauma. A naturalistic remitted depressed patients sample (N = 209) performed an Approach-Avoidance Task (AAT) with facial expressions (angry, sad, happy and neutral).
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree that the record is a completed empirical replication ('conceptual replication study') analyzing AAT, 5-HTTLPR genotype, and childhood trauma data in 209 remitted depressed patients to test whether earlier G x E intermediate-phenotype findings hold for automatic approach-avoidance tendencies.
